title: hashlib — Secure hashes and message digests — Python 3.14.7 documentation
excerpt:
hashlib
— Secure hashes and message digests
¶
Source code:
Lib/hashlib.py
This module implements a common interface to many different hash algorithms.
Included are the FIPS secure hash algorithms SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512,
(defined in
the FIPS 180-4 standard
), the SHA-3 series (defined in
the FIPS
202 standard
) as well as the legacy algorithms SHA1 (
formerly part of FIPS
)
and the MD5 algorithm (defined in internet
RFC 1321
).
Note
If you want the adler32 or crc32 hash functions, they are available in
the
zlib
module.
Hash algorithms
¶
There is one constructor method named for each type of
hash
.  All return
a hash object with the same simple interface. For example: use
sha256()
to create a SHA-256 hash object. You can now feed this object with
bytes-like objects
(normally
bytes
)
